cards.explanation: The answer is that he runs ahead and climbs a tree. Luke 19:4 says he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, since Jesus was about to pass that way. He figured out where Jesus was headed and got there first, friends. A man with a plan and a branch.

The reason Jesus gives is that He must stay at Zacchaeus's house today. Jesus says, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.” (Luke 19:5) Jesus is the one saying He will stay there. And He says it to the man up in the sycamore tree, who only wanted to see who Jesus was (Luke 19:3).

The word is joyfully. Luke 19:6 says Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed Him joyfully. Up in that tree he only wanted to see who Jesus was (Luke 19:3). I bet he never expected to be the one doing the welcoming, friends.

What the people say is, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!” (Luke 19:7) All who saw this began to grumble. The grumbling is about the guest list, friends. I think that's a lot of opinions about one visit.

The answer is half. Zacchaeus says, “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor…” (Luke 19:8) A very wealthy man, and half goes out the door. I've given away a cookie before and felt it, bakers. This is a whole different level.

The answer is that he will repay it fourfold. Zacchaeus says, “…if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.” (Luke 19:8) Fourfold means he pays back four times the amount. I couldn't even return a borrowed rolling pin on time, friends, so this humbles me.
The word is salvation. Jesus says, “Today salvation has come to this house…” (Luke 19:9) Today, not someday, friends. It came to the house of the man the crowd was grumbling about.

The reason Jesus gives is that this man too is a son of Abraham. He says, “…this man too is a son of Abraham.” (Luke 19:9) The people had called Zacchaeus a sinful man (Luke 19:7). Jesus calls him a son of Abraham.

The word is lost. Jesus says, “For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.” (Luke 19:10) Seek and save, friends. I sat in the back of a drawer for years, so this line gets me every time. Somebody came looking.
